items.title: VGN urges FG to equip vigilantes ahead of 2027 elections
items.description: By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Vigilante Group of Nigeria (VGN) has appealed to the Federal Government to provide protective kits and other equipment for its members following the killing of several vigilantes during operations against kidnappers, bandits and other criminal elements across the country. The group also unveiled its proposed security strategy for the 2027 general elections, saying its grassroots presence would be used to provide early-warning information and support to conventional security agencies. The Commandant-General and National Chairman of VGN, Otunba James Udoma, disclosed this on Wednesday in Abuja while briefing journalists on the group’s strategic security posture ahead of the 2027 elections. Udoma said the group’s election security framework was not intended to replace the Armed Forces, Nigeria Police Force, Department of State Services (DSS), Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps (NSCDC) or other statutory security agencies. He said the VGN would instead leverage its grassroots network to strengthen community-based intelligence and support lawful security interventions. “Our 2027 election security strategy is not designed to replace the Armed Forces, the Police, DSS, NSCDC or any statutory security institution. “It is designed to ensure that our grassroots presence becomes a responsible additional source of early-warning information and community support for the national security architecture,” he said. Udoma said VGN members would be required to operate within the law and maintain the confidence of the communities they serve. He warned that members who acted outside their lawful mandate would face disciplinary measures, adding that the organisation would not tolerate intimidation, extortion, harassment, impersonation, abuse of authority or partisan conduct. “Our loyalty is to Nigeria, the rule of law and the peaceful democratic process. We will protect the right of every citizen to participate peacefully in democracy, regardless of political affiliation,” he said. The VGN boss said its members would not intimidate voters, obstruct accredited election officials, participate in partisan activities or take the law into their own hands. He explained that where members witnessed security incidents, their responsibility would be to observe, report and support lawful intervention by competent authorities. Udoma said the organisation would strengthen its grassroots information network across states, local government areas, wards and communities to facilitate the rapid transmission of credible information to relevant authorities. According to him, the VGN is developing a 2027 Election Security Support and Community Intelligence Framework aimed at improving the flow of grassroots intelligence to conventional security agencies before, during and after the elections. He said the framework would also remain operational after the elections to help identify emerging tensions, threats to public order and other security concerns before they escalate. “Election security does not end when voting ends. The period immediately after elections can present its own security challenges,” he said. On political neutrality, Udoma said the VGN was not a political organisation and warned members against using the group’s uniforms, offices, vehicles, insignia or positions to campaign for political parties or candidates. “VGN is not a political party. Our members may have individual political preferences as citizens, but the organisation itself must remain politically neutral in the discharge of its security-support responsibilities,” he said. He also urged Nigerians not to be afraid of the 2027 elections, but to participate peacefully, respect the law, verify information before sharing it and report suspicious activities through appropriate channels. “We may belong to different political parties, but we belong to one Nigeria. Our democracy must be stronger than our political disagreements,” he said. Udoma called on commanders and members nationwide to embrace discipline and professionalism, while urging conventional security agencies to strengthen cooperation with the VGN where appropriate and lawful. He said the organisation’s approach ahead of the elections would be guided by the principles: “Observe. Report. Prevent. Support. Protect — within the law.” The Commandant-General further appealed to the Federal Government to support vigilantes with protective equipment, noting that members had continued to participate in operations against kidnapping, banditry and other crimes in several communities. He said adequate protection and equipment would enhance the ability of VGN personnel to support security agencies while reducing the risks faced by members during operations. Udoma assured Nigerians that the VGN remained committed to contributing its grassroots reach and experience to efforts to maintain peace, security and national unity before, during and after the 2027 general elections. The post VGN urges FG to equip vigilantes ahead of 2027 elections appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: La Fiscalía pide mantener la imputación de Jésica Rodríguez, expareja de Ábalos
items.description: La Fiscalía Anticorrupción no cede. Quiere que se mantenga la imputación de Jésica Rodríguez, antigua pareja del exministro de Transportes José Luis Ábalos, condenado a 24 años de cárcel por el caso mascarillas . La fiscal Carmen García Cerdá pide a la Sala de Apelación de la Audiencia Nacional que rechace el recurso que presentó Rodríguez y respalde la decisión que el pasado 3 de julio adoptó el instructor del caso Koldo , Ismael Moreno, de otorgarle la condición de investigada. El magistrado dio paso a petición del ministerio público y después de que el Tribunal Supremo considerase probado que la mujer fue enchufada en varias empresas públicas en las que cobró sin realizar trabajo alguno. items.title: 14 infants killed in fire at Pims' gynae ward in Islamabad
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Fourteen infants were killed in a fire that broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) early on Wednesday. Footage showed rescue workers using ladders to reach broken windows to access the affected area and grief-stricken women sitting on the ground outside the hospital. An AFP reporter saw a woman in tears and a man clear glass from two broken windows, as security guards stood at the entrance to the medical facility. Several witnesses, their hands and faces blackened from the smoke, told AFP they waited hours for help from the emergency services. They were forced to smash through windows to try and get to the neonatal intensive care unit. Others said they came across locked doors and alleged guards prevented those inside the building from leaving as the fire raged. However, the hospital disputed this in a statement issued later in the evening. “All emergency exits were fully open and operational,” it asserted. In a statement, the Islamabad administration said that the fire broke out on the third floor of the Mother and Child Hospital’s ward. It said that rescue teams rushed to the scene, with six fire brigade vehicles and four ambulances taking part in the rescue operation. “The fire was immediately brought under control and the children were immediately shifted to the intensive care unit,” it said, adding that 14 children “were completely burnt”. Pims Spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn that 15 babies were in the ward. “At least one baby was saved by a doctor,” she said. Health Minister Mustafa Kamal, who reached Islamabad from Karachi in the afternoon, vowed that “no one responsible for negligence, including me, will be spared”. “The tragic fire incident at Pims MCH Centre, resulting in the loss of precious neonatal lives, is deeply heartbreaking,” the public hospital said. Citing a preliminary report, the Pims statement said the incident was “initially caused by a spark inside nursery at 06:38am and within seconds a massive fire erupted due to oxygen points at each incubator”. It said two doctors and two nurses on duty inside the nursery responded “immediately and called security staff, who joined in and tried to get in twice [to bring] babies out until 06:39am, when a huge blast occurred and ceilings fell down”. The statement said the duty staff managed to rescue a baby in the nursery and four in an adjacent room, along with three mothers. “Besides immediate response, staff managed rescue of 73 other admitted patients in the adjacent Gynae ward on the same floor within minutes,” it added. The hospital asserted that “available fire safety equipment installed, including 35 fire extinguishers, were all utilised by the staff to contain the situation”. Health minister vows accountability Speaking to reporters in Islamabad, the health minister said he will present himself to his superiors for accountability. Providing details of the incident, Kamal said: “At 6:38am, it can be seen in the CCTV footage that there was a spark in the AC, then a fireball could be seen erupting out of it and landing on the floor of the ward. In one minute, at 6:39am, four people, including two nurses and two doctors, could be seen rushing for help and around the same time, the whole room was engulfed in flames”. The health minister said the incident was being investigated by “experts, different institutions including us”, adding that “nothing will remain hidden and all facts will be unearthed”. He continued: “Apparently, it seems that 14 out of the 15 infants were connected to oxygen tubes and it was that oxygen which caught flame.” Kamal reiterated that the “heart-wrenching” incident will be investigated and warned that “if there was any negligence, then as I said, we will not spare them, including myself”. The minister further said that Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif had instructed him “not to speak about certain issues”. He said he would be meeting the premier and that the two had been in touch. “Everyone is on board, and the findings will be presented,” he said. On being asked if he was going to tender his resignation, the health minister said, “As I have said before, whoever is responsible [..] they will not be spared. I have said what I can, and I wish I could say more, but the prime minister is my boss, and whatever his orders will be, I can only say that.” The federal minister was also questioned about fire safety standards at Pims, with a reporter pointing out that the hospital had been issued notices for the past eight years. Kamal claimed that the hospital had ensured compliance each time a notice had been issued in the past, pointing out that the blaze was contained with “26 fire extinguishers available in the building”. When a reporter asked about his early morning statement over the lack of adequate facilities at Pims and “why in his 2-2.5 years as a health minister, no improvement had been made”, the minister, getting visibly frustrated, said, “If it has been 2-2.5 years, then feel free to shoot me” and clarified that he had only been at his position for one year and two months. “What I said in the morning has to be seen within a certain parameter. I was saying that even if this did not happen, there are still challenges at the hospital. It has a capacity of 200-300 OPDs, and today, it has a footfall of over 9,000 people”. He maintained that he was merely presenting facts. “I am not saying that everything is ideal.” When pointed out that it was his responsibility to upgrade the facility, Kamal acknowledged his role and said, “We have to do it, but things cannot be ideal given the current scenario, but if we go into that, the conversation will take a different turn”. The minister reiterated that every responsible person will be held accountable. “If I am willing to present myself for accountability, then no one else is left. “Wherever there has been negligence, we will fix it,” he said. Noting that such an incident should not have happened, he said: “Will get to its root cause and ensure prevention in the future.” The minister was also asked about reports that the door of the ward was locked, to which he said that access to the ward was limited and guarded due to “instances of people stealing newborn babies a couple of years back”. “You would not see that anywhere else in the world, but we have the issue, so the door had to be manned with a guard,” Kamal explained. During his media talk, the minister got into a verbal altercation with an individual who asked when action would be taken against those responsible. As the individual got louder, the minister repeatedly gestured to him to come forward and said, “Sir, come here and talk to me.” ‘Give me my child back’ Malik Israr, whose niece was admitted to the gynae ward, told Dawn that it was unfortunate the nursery was housed in a building in which repair and renovation work was ongoing. “After the fire erupted, they told patients to vacate the building. Women who had just given birth had to rush down the stairs from the second floor,” he said. A worker removes broken pieces of a glass window after a fire broke out at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — Reuters Khurram Mehmood, 40, told AFP he lost his three-day-old daughter in the blaze and that rescuers took hours to arrive. “I lost my daughter. She was only three days old,” he said. “My wife was in the ward. They took everyone out. We were sitting on the road waiting for help.” He added, “The fire erupted at 6am, rescue and authorities reached at 9am; people were helping themselves.” “Give me my child back,” Jaweria, who lost her newborn, said outside the hospital. “I want justice.” She told AFP : “Rescue teams arrived too late. Police arrived after four hours and said they are here to investigate. To hell with you, rescue team and police. Babies burnt to death there, but nobody could save them.” Jaweria (2nd R), who said she lost her child in the fire, reacts following the blaze at the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP “For two hours I kept crying and wailing,” the mother said, questioning the action taken by hospital staff and emergency responders. “Why did the doctors leave the children there? One nurse, one doctor, one gynaecologist, one paediatrician — there was nobody in the entire ward. Why were they not there?” Mudasir, another parent who also lost his child, said all doors of the ward, except one, were shut and that there was “no fire security” in the ward. A mother with black residue from the smoke on her hands stood crying outside the hospital as she held her 10-day-old baby in her arms. “People were screaming. There was black smoke. We ran for our lives. Thank god my baby is safe,” Shagufta Parveen told AFP . A man consoles a grieving father (C) as his child’s coffin is carried after a fire outside the Mother and Child Health (MCH) ward at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (Pims) hospital in Islamabad on Aug 26, 2026. — AFP Ali Abbas, 20, was with his sister who was a patient in the ward. “There was a short circuit in the nursery, in the children’s ward,” he said. “It was full of smoke.” Eyewitness Abdul Ghafoor told AFP that there was “thick black smoke inside and patients were trapped”. “I barged in to try to save as many people as I could, but we could not reach the ward where the patients were. “The fire was in the nursing room, and we could not see anything. Some of us broke the windows to help people get out.” Among the victims were the twin daughters of Bahadur Khan, a vegetable seller, The New York Times reported . He had left them with their mother to get some rest at home. Bahadur said his wife was recovering in Pims’ intensive care unit and was not aware of the deaths of their three-day-old daughters. Alam Zaib, the father of a newborn child who was in another ward and remained safe, was quoted as saying that he tried to enter the ward where the fire broke out, but the door was locked. Pims, established in 1985, is Islamabad’s biggest public sector hospital. It is one of the oldest health facilities in the federal capital and comprises several hospitals and teaching institutes. Fires in large buildings are frequent in Pakistan, often due to poor safety laws and building codes as well as lax enforcement. Federal health secretary removed Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif took notice of the incident and directed the relevant authorities to investigate it. According to the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO), he expressed deep sorrow and grief at the incident and offered his condolences to the bereaved families. “Such a situation involving children is unbearable,” the statement quoted him as saying. “The circumstances that led to the incident should be thoroughly reviewed, those responsible should be identified, and the strictest possible action should be taken,” he said. In a second statement, the PMO said the prime minister had suspended and removed federal Health Secretary Muhammad Aslam Ghauri. The premier chaired a high-level meeting on the incident, where he expressed his anger and issued directives for “strict action”, the PMO said in another statement. It also stated that the prime minister suspended the federal health secretary and asked him to leave the meeting. The statement quoted the prime minister as saying: “I am heartbroken at this tragic incident and share the parents’ grief.” Subsequently, Captain (retired) Muhammad Mahmood, a BS-21 officer of the Pakistan Administrative Service (PAS), was appointed to the post of health secretary for three months “or till the posting of a regular incumbent,” a notification issued by the Cabinet Secretariat said. According to the PMO, a high-level inquiry committee, headed by former interior secretary Shahid Khan, has launched an investigation. State-run APP reported that Establishment Division Secretary Dr Barrister Nabeel Awan was also included in the committee. Further, a notification issued by the Islamabad district magistrate said that a fact-finding committee, headed by the additional deputy commissioner general (ADCG), had been formed to determine the facts behind the fire. The members of the committee included the CES director general, the City police station superintendent, the assistant commissioner (Industrial Area), the director general of Capital Development Authority’s (CDA) Electrical and Mechanical wing, along with representatives from Pims and Islamabad Electric Supply Company. The committee was tasked with determining the exact cause of the fire, assessing whether adequate and functional fire-safety measures were in place, and evaluating the response time and effectiveness of the rescue and fire-fighting operations. The notification said that a report would be furnished within 24 hours. Ambulances are parked outside a mortuary following a deadly fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad on August 26, 2026. — AFP Minister of State for Law Barrister Aqeel Malik assured in a post on X that a “complete, transparent, and impartial investigation of the incident will be conducted to determine the true causes of this catastrophe and any possible negligence”. “In the event that negligence or failure is proven at any level, strict action will be taken against the responsible individuals in accordance with the law,” he added, extending his condolences to the bereaved families and expressing grief over the incident. Meanwhile, PPP leader Nayyar Hussain Bokhari, who reached Pims along with Senator Sherry Rehman and others, demanded that the head of the MCH be removed. Bokhari said it was not just negligence but rather criminal negligence and should not be ignored. Rehman said the Pims’ executive director must “answer why the system here keeps being akin to gross negligence”. “The health ministry now has no justification for taking public funds. It should be dissolved or devolved to the provinces,” she was quoted as saying by her party. She insisted they were not visiting “to play politics” but were sent by the party leadership to raise questions on behalf of the public. In a post on her X account, Rehman also shared a video of her visiting the ward. “Totally gutted. People had to break windows and jump out. Emergency gate was closed, fire equipment not working, medical staff not present,” she wrote. “Honestly, I would have resigned on the spot,” Rehman added later. Tallal Chaudhry defends district administration Minister of State for Interior Tallal Chaudhry insisted that there had not been any delay in the arrival of rescue teams and defended the district administration. “After receiving information in the control room, they reached the hospital within six minutes,” the state minister said while speaking to the media in Islamabad. He added that once the rescue teams assessed the situation, 19 people were rescued, including seven children, 1o mothers and two men. He also said that administration officials “from the assistant commissioner to commissioner to the Islamabad IG” reached the hospital to monitor the situation. “Not only did they monitor but also assisted in the rescue operation,” he said. Reiterating that rescue teams reached the site within six minutes, the state minister said, “There appears to be no negligence on the part of rescue services.” However, he added, only the hospital administration could answer for the arrangements present within the hospital. Chaudhry said that the bodies of all 14 infants had been handed over to their families. He added that a report of the incident had been sent to the prime minister and Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, who he said had been monitoring the situation. On being asked if Pims met the CDA’s fire safety protocols, with a journalist also pointing out that his ministry had been issuing notices to the hospital for the past seven years, he acknowledged that notices had been issued. “It is a huge institution, and notices were issued […] but what was complied with and what was not — as there are multiple buildings; we cannot conclude anything today, and an inquiry committee has been formed”. Asked why the administration had not been active on the fire safety issue before, he said, “If there has been any negligence, the inquiry committee will find out.” An inquiry committee has been formed for a “high-powered” investigation into the incident, Chaudhry noted. He said the committee will collect evidence — CCTV footage, presence of flammable equipment, why the door was locked, the number of doctors and nurses present — and present its findings. In its update on the incident, CDA said fire and rescue teams reached the site within seven minutes after a call was received at 6:54am. Fire tenders, rescue teams, ambulances of the Capital Emergency Services (CES) and the Islamabad Capital Territory (ICT) administration were part of the deployed resources. Nation expresses grief President Asif Ali Zardari expressed heartfelt condolences and sympathy to the bereaved families. In a statement, the president said that the loss of lives was “heartbreaking and an irreparable loss”. “Responsibility for the incident should be determined and action should be taken in accordance with the law,” he said. Effective fire safety and emergency arrangements must be ensured in hospitals for the protection of patients, especially newborn babies, the president urged. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said he was deeply saddened by the incident. “My deepest condolences to the bereaved parents and families. No words can ease the pain of losing an innocent child. May Allah Almighty grant the families strength and sabr in this unimaginably difficult hour,” he said. As per the prime minister’s orders an immediate and thorough investigation will establish the causes of this tragic incident to ensure that those found responsible face the strictest action. The safety of our children must remain paramount,” he said. PPP Chairman Bilawal Bhutto-Zardari wrote on X: “Mothers do not keep their children in the womb for nine months just so that, due to someone’s negligence, they burn alive as soon as they are born. “The deaths of 14 newborns in the federal capital are one of the most horrific tragedies in human history. The helpless fathers, whose lamps of hope were extinguished the very instant they were lit, are seeking justice.” In a statement earlier in the day, he described the incident as an “unbearable tragedy for the entire nation”. He called for an impartial investigation into the incident and said the nation be informed how such a tragedy occurred at a major hospital. “Those responsible for negligence or failing to ensure the safety of patients must be held accountable,” he added, stressing that the federal government must ensure the safety of patients and medical staff at all hospitals under its administration. First Lady and MNA Aseefa Bhutto-Zardari also expressed “profound grief and sorrow over the tragic loss of newborn babies” and conveyed her “deepest sympathies to the bereaved families”. “The loss of innocent newborn lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing,” a statement by the Presidency quoted her as saying. She called for a “thorough, swift and transparent investigation” into the incident. PML-N President Nawaz Sharif said he was “deeply grieved” to hear about the deaths. He urged the government to take strict action against those responsible and ensure measures were put in place to prevent such incidents in the future. Senate Chairman Syed Yousuf Raza Gilani expressed deep grief and sorrow over the tragic incident. In a statement, he offered his condolences to the families affected. He said effective safety measures, fire safety systems and all necessary arrangements to deal with emergencies must be ensured in hospitals to prevent such incidents. “Any negligence in safety measures is unacceptable,” he said. Gilani urged the relevant authorities to conduct a comprehensive investigation into the incident and take effective and practical steps to prevent such tragedies in the future. National Assembly Speaker Sardar Ayaz Sadiq also expressed profound grief and sorrow over the deaths of the infants. In a statement, he said he was “heartbroken” over the incident and shared equally in the pain and grief of the bereaved parents. United Nations International Children’s Emergency Fund (Unicef) called for an urgent review as it expressed grief over the incident. “Unicef is deeply saddened by the tragic loss of at least 14 newborn lives following a fire at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences hospital in Islamabad today. “We extend our deepest condolences to the bereaved families and all those affected by this devastating incident,” it said in a statement. The UN agency added, “ Every newborn deserves a safe start to life, and every mother and child should be able to receive care in a safe, secure health facility. It called for the urgent review and strengthening of fire prevention and safety standards across health facilities. The British High Commission in Pakistan termed the incident “heartbreaking news”. “Our deepest condolences and thoughts are with the parents and families at this unimaginably difficult time,” it said. Saudi Arabia’s Foreign Ministry also expressed “deepest condolences and sincere sympathy” to the families of the infants and to the people and the government of Pakistan. “The kingdom expresses its solidarity with the families of the victims and stands with the government and people of Pakistan in the face of this great tragedy, wishing the Islamic Republic of Pakistan and its brotherly people security and peace,” the statement read. The Turkish embassy said it was “deeply saddened by the tragic loss of newborn lives”, “We extend our heartfelt condolences and deepest sympathies to the bereaved families. Our thoughts and prayers are with them at this profoundly painful time. May Allah grant them strength, patience and solace,” it said on X. Spain’s embassy also extended heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families. “Our thoughts are with all those affected by this heartbreaking tragedy.” The French embassy shared the sentiment, describing the incident as “deeply distressing”. “Our hearts go out to the families who lost their newborn children in the tragic fire at Pims in Islamabad. Loss of innocent lives is heartbreaking and deeply distressing. Embassy of France extends its deepest sympathies to bereaved families and everyone affected by this tragedy,” it said in its message on X. The Pakistan Medical Association (PMA) said in a statement that it was in “deep mourning” over the incident. “The association reiterates that healthcare facilities are designed to protect and restore human lives, yet administrative failure and regulatory oversight lapses have turned these institutions into danger zones,” it said. It demanded action against officials “whose failure to uphold safety codes resulted in this catastrophe”. It also demanded enforcing strict consequences so that “systemic failure serves as a decisive warning, preventing future lapses across both public and private medical facilities”. It further said that there should be immediate restructuring and public accountability of health regulatory authorities responsible for enforcing safety protocols, building codes and emergency infrastructure in hospitals. The PMA also called for “full institutional backing for the grieving parents, ensuring they receive complete legal, financial, and emotional justice”. Search for Justice (SFJ) and Children Advocacy Network (CAN) Pakistan, a collective platform of local civil society organisations working for the protection and rights of children, also expressed their deep sorrow. “The death of newborn children in a place entrusted with their treatment and care is deeply distressing and raises serious questions about safety and emergency preparedness,” said Rashida Qureshi, programme manager at SFJ and spokesperson for CAN Pakistan. In its statement, the Islamabad Citizens Network (ICN) said, “This is not merely an unfortunate accident; it is a national tragedy in which innocent newborns, entirely dependent on the hospital system, its staff and state-provided arrangements for their safety and survival, lost their lives.” It contended that an inquiry committee headed by an ADC was “neither adequate nor appropriate given the gravity of the tragedy and the need to determine possible administrative, criminal and institutional responsibility”. ICN demanded an immediate judicial inquiry and an independent investigation into allegations by parents regarding the absence of staff, emergency exits and other administrative lapses. It recalled that similar tragic incidents had occurred in Lahore’s Services Hospital in June 2012, the National Institute of Child Health (NICH) in Karachi in January 2020, and the nursery of Sahiwal Teaching Hospital in June 2024. Civil Society Network Pakistan (CSNP) called upon Federal Constitution Court’s (FCC) Chief Justice Aminuddin Khan to take immediate notice on a suo motu basis or initiate appropriate constitutional proceedings on serious human rights violations arising out of the babies’ deaths. CSNP President Advocate Abdullah Malik told Dawn that he has also requested the FCC chief justice to consider constituting a high-level, independent and transparent inquiry to determine the exact cause and circumstances of the fire at Pims. Additional input from AFP, Reuters and Nasir Iqbal

items.title: « Prospective géopolitique française en Afrique Noire francophone postindépendance » – 4 questions à Aboubakar Ouattara
items.description: Aboubakar Ouattara est conférencier, sémanticien des langues, de la communication verbale et non verbale, analyste en géopolitique et prospective. Il a dirigé le département de français de l’Université de Tromsø en Norvège. Il répond aux questions de Pascal Boniface à l’occasion de la parution de son ouvrage Prospective géopolitique française en Afrique Noire francophone postindépendance aux éditions L'Harmattan. Pour vous, la période de De Gaulle à Chirac, donc de 1958 à 2007, a été l'âge d'or de la France-Afrique… Oui. La triade terminologique âge d’or , âge d’argent et âge de plomb usitée dans le livre est inspirée d’Hésiode. [1] Elle nous a paru juste pour caractériser le continuum géopolitique de la France-Afrique, de De Gaulle à Chirac, puis de Sarkozy à Hollande, et enfin à Macron. La force de prestige sémantique de chacun des trois métaux est métaphoriquement associée à la période géopolitique qui lui correspond sur le continuum. Il suit de là que, du point de vue des intérêts de la France, de De Gaulle à Macron, l’histoire de la France-Afrique est celle d’une dégradation progressive en termes de tendance lourde. Que cette histoire soit dénommée France-Afrique, Françafrique, Afrique-France, Africa-France ou Africa Forward, le trait de sens fédérateur involué dans ces appellations est la relation de puissance qu’elles instituent entre les acteurs concernés : la France et les pays d’Afrique. En termes de géopolitique, l'âge d'or de la France-Afrique signifie, pour la France, avoir le contrôle ; avoir la capacité effective d’exercer sur l’autre acteur les leviers du soft et/ou du hard power à disposition afin d’aligner ce dernier dans le sens des intérêts de la France, prioritairement. Il n’est pas déplacé de dire que, structurellement, ce contrôle a fonctionné à son rendement maximal de De Gaulle à Chirac « le dernier des gaullistes » [2] , c’est-à-dire du deal de l’indépendance-association avec ses accords dits spéciaux au postulat et code de conduite géopolitiques énoncés par Chirac à l’endroit des dirigeants d’Afrique noire francophone : « Si vous voulez l’appui de la France, sachez respecter docilement les règles que vous savez » [3] . Peut-on parler de dégradation ou de renouvellement pour les quinquennats de Nicolas Sarkozy et de François Hollande ? Les quinquennats de Nicolas Sarkozy et de François Hollande accusent un renouvellement de surface sur fond de fidélité à l’esprit de l’âge d’or ; ce qui les a empêchés de favoriser une relation partenariale avec les pays d’Afrique noire francophone. Sinon, comment expliquer les écarts de comportements grossiers de la politique étrangère de la France sous chacun des deux quinquennats à l’endroit de ces pays — écarts qui sont des marqueurs et accélérateurs de la dégradation de la relation France-Afrique ? Les exemples sont légion. Du côté du quinquennat de Nicolas Sarkozy, on peut citer le non-respect de sa promesse de rupture, son discours à l’Université de Dakar, les interventions militaires au Tchad, en Côte d’Ivoire (et même en Libye étant donné les effets induits de cette dernière intervention sur l’espace africain francophone). Du côté du quinquennat de François Hollande, on peut citer son injonction aux dirigeants africains « à opérer l’inéluctable changement » ; ce qui a été vécu par certains d’entre eux comme « une greffe, un acte imposé ». [4] Pour ces deux quinquennats, on ne peut pas parler de dégradation ou de renouvellement. Je parlerai de dégradation et de renouvellement . J’observe que le renouvellement est superficiel par rapport à la logique de l’âge d’or qui répond d’une tendance structurelle. Les marqueurs de dégradation sont réels. Ils nourrissent le dévissement de la France dans la relation. Et cela, dans un environnement stratégique global favorable aux pays africains quant à une refondation de la relation France-Afrique. Qu'est-ce qui change avec Emmanuel Macron ? Ce sont trois choses : 1. l’accélération de la dégradation de la relation en défaveur de la France ; 2. l’ampleur et l’intensité du rejet de la France par des dirigeants africains, par des élites africaines (intellectuelles, médiatiques, politiques), par des entrepreneurs africains face à la concurrence déloyale avec les grands groupes français, par une certaine classe moyenne africaine qui s’informe quotidiennement sur les relations entre la France et les pays africains et sur l’évolution des relations internationales et géopolitiques dans le monde, par une certaine classe populaire africaine connectée sur les réseaux sociaux et sur les chaînes de télévision satellitaires françaises ; 3. ce qui change c’est aussi l’itération des outrances verbales et non-verbales. Elles sont liées à la psychologie transgressive de Macron et sont légion. Elles incluent la convocation des présidents du G5 Sahel à Pau (16 décembre 2019 / 11 janvier 2020), l’accusation d’« ingratitude » portée contre les gouvernants africains lors de son discours aux ambassadeurs de France à l’Élysée (6 janvier 2025). Mais ne soyons pas dupes de ses outrances. Emmanuel Macron choisit ses victimes. Ses dérapages confirment son alliance avec le principe de l’âge d’or. Pensez-vous que les 13 propositions d'Achille Mbembe donnent la possibilité d'une « conversion des regards » ? Je pense que les 13 propositions ne donnent que la possibilité superficielle sans plus. L’état des regards, avant les 13 propositions, offre le constat d’un déséquilibre essentiel dans la relation, une inégalité structurelle. L’exégèse des 13 propositions censées favoriser la « conversion des regards » nous a conduit au statu quo ante . Ce constat confère au corpus des 13 propositions un rôle cosmétique : Le corpus reflète un projet de réformes pour faire évoluer certaines propriétés de la relation, en témoignage de changement, mais pas la relation elle-même qui reste irremplacée dans son existence même, c’est-à-dire dans sa raison d’être géopolitique, prédatrice, inégale, fidèle au souffle vital de l’âge d’or. Le projet de refondation cristallisé dans les propositions n’est pas un projet de rupture. Le corpus est verrouillé pour ne rester que dans l’axe de la continuation de la relation inégalitaire, mais il est vendu comme un événement géopolitique refondateur. Le corpus reste un adjuvant de géopolitique prospective pour la consolidation de la présence de la France comme puissance en Afrique noire francophone afin d’y préserver durablement ses intérêts. Plus largement, afin de satisfaire sa volonté de puissance, de rang et d’influence à l’échelle globale. L’angle mort du rapport d’Achille Mbembe réside dans son évitement à penser la question de la souveraineté des pays d’Afrique noire francophone hors d’un couplage inféodant avec la France. Achille Mbembe préfère intégrer la souveraineté de ces pays dans celle de la France et, au-delà, dans celle de l’Europe. Il croit au mariage du pot de fer avec le pot de terre et fait mine d’ignorer la mémoire de leur histoire partagée, historien de son état. Les 13 propositions d'Achille Mbembe donnent la possibilité d'une « conversion des regards » qui est une conversion de surface du type des conversions où tout doit changer pour que rien ne change. Et à ce jeu de ruse géopolitique, la France (ses alliés avec) possède une expertise avérée. L’histoire de ses relations avec les États d’Afrique francophone regorge d’exemples. À titre d’illustration, pensons à la geste qui part du tournant vers les indépendances en juin 1943 (avec la Constitution du Comité français de Libération nationale à Alger sous l’autorité du Général de Gaulle) jusqu’au sommet Africa Forward en mai 2026. Passons-y la tenue de la Conférence africaine française de Brazzaville en janvier 1944, la Création de l’Union française en octobre 1946, le Vote de la loi-cadre, dite Defferre, en juin 1956, la Communauté franco-africaine créée dans le cadre de la nouvelle Constitution française en 1958 et l’accession massive aux indépendances en 1960. La liste intérieure à l’intervalle de temps choisi est plus longue… Rien que de la ruse géopolitique. [1] In Les Travaux et les Jours , VIII e siècle av. J.-C. [2] Nous tenons cette périphrase de Dominique de Villepin, Mémoire de paix pour temps de guerre, Grasset, Paris, 2016, p. 18 : « La foi inébranlable dans la vocation de la France et l’esprit de combat ont fait de lui, sur la scène internationale, le dernier des Gaullistes ». On retrouve la même idée chez Francis Laloupo, France – Afrique. La rupture maintenant ?, Acoria éditions, Paris, 2013, p. 24 : « Après François Mitterrand, Jacques Chirac sera l’homme qui déploiera, jusqu’à la caricature, toutes les traditions et pratiques de la Françafrique. L’Histoire conférera à Chirac un statut particulier : celui du « dernier homme ». Le dernier chef d’État français à avoir placé l’Afrique au centre de ses œuvres présidentielles. » ; « Chirac sera donc le « dernier homme », le dernier de la génération des chefs d’État français à avoir mis au cœur de la gestion du pouvoir l’équation africaine » (ibid., p. 26) ; « Après le règne du dernier homme, Nicolas Sarkozy disposait des atouts nécessaires pour opérer la rupture générationnelle » (ibid., p. 27-28). [3] Cité par Francis Laloupo, ibid., p. 24-25. [4] Les segments guillemetés sont empruntés à Francis Laloupo, ibid., p.137. L’article « Prospective géopolitique française en Afrique Noire francophone postindépendance » – 4 questions à Aboubakar Ouattara est apparu en premier sur IRIS .

items.title: Southern, Middle Belt leaders reject proposed cattle ranching scheme
items.description: …Demand transparency on land acquisition, ownership, beneficiaries …Warn FG against imposing livestock policy on communities By Henry Umoru, Abuja Leaders of the Southern and Middle Belt Leaders Forum (SMBLF) have rejected any attempt to compulsorily allocate community lands in the Middle Belt and southern parts of the country for cattle ranching. The leaders, comprising representatives of Afenifere, Ohanaeze Ndigbo Worldwide, the Pan Niger Delta Forum (PANDEF) and the Middle Belt Forum (MBF), said they were opposed to what they described as an opaque approach to the Federal Government’s proposed livestock policy. In a statement signed on Wednesday by the Chairman of the SMBLF and leader of Afenifere, Oba Oladipo Olaitan; President-General of Ohanaeze Ndigbo Worldwide, Senator John Azuta-Mbata; National Chairman of PANDEF, Ambassador Godknows Igali; and President of the Middle Belt Forum, Dr Bitrus Pogu, the group demanded full disclosure of the government’s plans. The proposed areas, according to the leaders, include Nasarawa, Plateau, Benue, Southern Kaduna, Taraba and the Federal Capital Territory. The SMBLF said it was particularly concerned about what it described as the concentration of the proposed pilot scheme in the Middle Belt, despite the availability of large areas of sparsely populated land in other parts of the country. “The Southern and Middle Belt Leaders Forum (SMBLF) is alarmed by the audacious attempt by the Federal Government to take over lands belonging to ethnic communities in the Middle Belt under a spurious ‘pilot scheme’ being introduced in the name of a New National Livestock Policy,” the statement said. The group stressed that it was not opposed to modern livestock production, ranching or the development of the livestock value chain, but rejected what it described as a coercive and discriminatory approach to land allocation. “What we reject is the opaque, coercive and discriminatory manner in which this policy is being pursued to the exclusive advantage of nomadic Fulani herdsmen,” it said. The leaders warned that any pilot scheme implemented without the consent and protection of affected communities could eventually be extended to other parts of the country. They also said the Federal Government should clarify the legal basis for acquiring the proposed lands, arguing that the Land Use Act should not be interpreted as a blanket authority for arbitrary acquisition of community lands. “The Federal Government must be reminded that the Land Use Act of 1978 is not a licence for arbitrary land grabbing,” the statement said. The SMBLF argued that ranching was primarily an economic enterprise and questioned the use of compulsory acquisition powers for the benefit of specific economic interests. The leaders further expressed concerns about the security and demographic implications of establishing permanent settlements through the livestock policy, citing previous proposals such as Rural Grazing Areas (RUGA) and cattle colonies, which generated widespread controversy. The group said it stood with the Middle Belt Forum in rejecting the proposed scheme and called on communities and governments in the southern states to remain vigilant over any plans involving their lands. The leaders demanded full disclosure of the proposed ranching locations, the legal instruments backing their acquisition, ownership arrangements, beneficiaries, size of the lands, security implications and funding sources. They said the government must answer the questions transparently and guarantee the rights of affected communities before proceeding with the policy. “We warn the Federal Government that the Middle Belt and the South are not dumping grounds for controversial land policies. Our lands belong to our communities that depend on them for farming, homes, livelihoods and survival,” they said. The SMBLF maintained that it would oppose any attempt to take over community lands under the guise of livestock development, while reiterating that it supported legitimate efforts to modernise Nigeria’s livestock sector. The post Southern, Middle Belt leaders reject proposed cattle ranching scheme appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: ‎NSMQ 2026: Keta SHTS secures quarterfinals spot after beating Anum Presby, Kadjebi Asato
items.description: Keta SHTS has kept its place among the seeded schools after a commanding performance against Anum Presby SHS and Kadjebi Asato SHS in the One-Eighth stage of the 2026 National Science and Maths Quiz (NSMQ). Keta SHTS set the pace from the first round, opening with 24 points as Anum Presby managed 17 points and Kadjebi Asato 9 points. By Round Two, Keta had stretched its lead to 43 points, with Anum Presby on 15 points and Kadjebi Asato on 12 points. ‎ ‎Anum Presby found some consolation on the Problem of the Day, scoring 6 out of 10, while Keta and Kadjebi Asato failed to score. The development, however, did little to change the contest as Keta SHTS remained firmly in control through Round Three. ‎ ‎Keta responded in Round Four, taking its tally to 53 points before finishing with 56 points. Anum Presby finished with 28 points, while Kadjebi Asato finished with 19 points. ‎Despite the difficult Round Three, Keta says it considers the setback a useful preparation for the quarter-finals and will return stronger. For Anum Presby and Kadjebi Asato, the result brings their 2026 NSMQ campaigns to an end, with both schools set to begin the journey again from the regional stage next year. items.title: Cyanure : six tonnes et une filière à remonter
items.description: © Internet Deux opérations douanières ont permis de saisir 6,1 tonnes de cyanure en deux mois. Au-delà des cargaisons interceptées, l’enquête doit maintenant remonter les circuits d’approvisionnement et identifier leurs destinataires. Dans la nuit du 22 août, vers 1 h 30, la Brigade mobile d’intervention des Douanes a découvert à Badalabougou 22 sacs contenant 1 100 kilogrammes de cyanure. Cette interception survient exactement deux mois après une saisie beaucoup plus importante effectuée à Sécoro, dans la région de Ségou. Le 22 juin, les douaniers avaient retrouvé 100 sacs de 50 kilogrammes, soit environ cinq tonnes, dans un véhicule. La marchandise avait été dissimulée sous des cartons de poissons séchés et des colis de tapis. Les deux opérations portent à 6,1 tonnes le volume de cyanure retiré de circuits présentés comme frauduleux. Le cyanure n’est pas interdit dans tous ses usages. Il est employé légalement dans certaines activités industrielles, notamment pour le traitement du minerai d’or. Son importation au Mali est néanmoins soumise à une autorisation des services des Mines ou de la Santé. Son transport, son stockage et son utilisation nécessitent des précautions strictes. Traçabilité Une exposition importante au cyanure peut empêcher l’organisme d’utiliser correctement l’oxygène et provoquer rapidement des atteintes au cerveau, au cœur et aux poumons. Une cargaison transportée sans documents, sans emballage approprié ou sans dispositif d’intervention constitue donc un risque pour les manutentionnaires, les riverains et les milieux naturels. Les saisies apportent une réponse immédiate, mais elles ne suffisent pas à démanteler une filière. Les Douanes n’ont pas encore publié l’origine de la cargaison de Badalabougou, sa destination, l’identité de ses propriétaires ou les autorisations éventuellement présentées. Aucun élément public ne permet donc d’affirmer qu’elle était destinée à un site minier déterminé. Une étude publiée en 2021 par la Global Initiative Against Transnational Organized Crime avait déjà décrit l’expansion, en Afrique de l’Ouest, de circuits clandestins alimentant certains sites d’extraction artisanale. Ce constat régional apporte un contexte, mais ne prouve pas que les cargaisons saisies en 2026 empruntaient les mêmes itinéraires. L’enjeu est désormais de retracer les achats, les moyens de paiement, les transporteurs, les entrepôts et les bénéficiaires finaux. Une investigation associant Douanes, Mines, Santé, Environnement et services judiciaires permettrait de dépasser le simple décompte des sacs. Les autorités devraient également préciser les conditions de conservation et de destruction des produits saisis. Pour une substance aussi dangereuse, la sécurisation après interception est aussi importante que l’opération douanière elle-même.

items.title: Police bust cybercrime syndicates over N3.62bn investment fraud, romance scams
items.description: …Arrest suspects in Lagos, Kano, Anambra, Ekiti over alleged cybercrimes By Kingsley Omonobi ABUJA — The Nigeria Police Force National Cybercrime Centre (NPF-NCCC) has arrested several suspects in separate investigations into alleged cyber-enabled crimes, including an international investment fraud involving suspected proceeds of about N3.62 billion. The Centre also arrested suspects over alleged romance scams, sextortion, business email compromise, identity theft, impersonation and the alleged theft and attempted sale of property belonging to a former employer. The Assistant Inspector-General of Police in charge of the NPF-NCCC, AIG Akaninyene Ezima, disclosed this on Wednesday while briefing journalists in Abuja. Ezima said the Centre’s investigations had uncovered sophisticated cybercrime operations involving victims in Nigeria and several other countries. N3.62bn investment fraud According to him, the investigation into the alleged investment fraud followed a petition over the loss of N56.29 million by victims who were allegedly lured into a WhatsApp-based stock trading platform with promises of high returns. He said operatives arrested Kelechi Sistus Ihekaire, proprietor of Kestart Technology, in Lagos on August 13. Ezima said forensic examination of devices recovered from the suspect revealed extensive digital records connected to the alleged operation. He said approximately N3.62 billion in suspected proceeds of crime was allegedly converted into Tether (USDT) stablecoins through Bybit peer-to-peer transactions. “Ihekaire was arrested in Lagos on August 13 and allegedly admitted ownership of Kestart Technology and involvement in peer-to-peer cryptocurrency trading on Bybit,” he said. The police said they would pursue legal processes for the forfeiture of funds under lien in the company’s account and associated cryptocurrency assets, with a view to facilitating victim restitution where applicable. Suspected romance scammer arrested Ezima also disclosed the arrest of Abdulwajeed Abdullahi, who allegedly operated under the pseudonym “Captain Junaid”, over an alleged romance scam and sextortion. He said the suspect was arrested in Kano on August 4 following a petition by a female victim. According to him, Abdullahi allegedly contacted the woman on TikTok before moving the conversation to WhatsApp, where he developed a romantic relationship with her and allegedly persuaded her to send intimate photographs and videos. The police said he subsequently demanded $3,000 and threatened to release the materials if she failed to pay. “Further investigation identified another victim, also reported losing N3,500,000 to the same ‘Captain Junaid’ identity,” Ezima said. He added that another female victim from Bauchi State allegedly paid the suspect $1,500 under a purported foreign exchange trading arrangement. Forensic examination of devices recovered from Abdullahi allegedly revealed intimate photographs and videos belonging to multiple women, as well as forged academic certificates and identity cards bearing his photograph but different names. Ezima said the suspect allegedly confessed to commencing romance scam activities in January 2026 and admitted using the identity and publicly available photographs of a Saudi pilot, “Captain Abdullahi Rajhi”, to create the fake persona. BEC suspect arrested in Lekki The AIG further disclosed the arrest of David Adeyemi Temitope in Lagos over an alleged sophisticated Business Email Compromise (BEC) operation. He said the suspect was arrested at his residence in Megamound Estate, Lekki, on July 20, following an investigation conducted in collaboration with foreign law enforcement agencies under the Budapest Convention 24/7 Network. According to Ezima, forensic examination of devices recovered from the suspect revealed email records linked to alleged victims in more than 50 countries, including Canada, Germany, the United States, India, France and the Netherlands. He said the suspect’s Bank Verification Number was linked to accounts with six financial institutions and fintech platforms, including GTBank, Zenith Bank, FairMoney, Carbon, OPay and PalmPay. A Mercedes-Benz AMG GLC 43, suspected to have been acquired with proceeds of crime, was also recovered. “The investigation further established that the suspect made in excess of N100 million from the criminal enterprise,” Ezima said. He explained that the suspect allegedly used phishing kits obtained from a vendor on Telegram to compromise Microsoft 365 login credentials belonging to employees of targeted companies. Two arrested over identity theft In another case, the police arrested Emeka Egba Anthony, 28, and Ogboji Solomon Emeka, 29, in Anambra State over alleged conspiracy, identity theft, impersonation and computer-related fraud. The arrests followed a complaint by a senior civil servant who alleged that his identity had been stolen and used on WhatsApp and Facebook. Ezima said operatives arrested the suspects on August 4 and recovered 24 registered and 33 unregistered MTN SIM cards, 26 registered and 18 unregistered Airtel SIM cards, as well as an MTN toolkit from Anthony. He said Anthony allegedly admitted being a registered toolkit operator with MTN and Airtel and engaging in the sale of registered and unregistered SIM cards. He also allegedly admitted creating a social media profile using the identity of “Catherine Harry”, purportedly a UK citizen, to defraud individuals in India. The second suspect, Ogboji, allegedly admitted dealing in pre-registered SIM cards, which the police said could facilitate identity theft, impersonation and other cybercrimes. Suspected impersonator arrested The Centre also arrested Babatunde Olamilekan Idowu, popularly known as “CSP Bamiseye”, over alleged impersonation of a serving Commissioner of Police at the Force Criminal Investigation Department, Abuja. According to Ezima, the suspect and other members of the alleged syndicate, who remain at large, purportedly impersonated senior police and government officials to defraud a victim of N17 million. He said Idowu allegedly posed as CSP Bamiseye, while other members of the group allegedly impersonated the Inspector-General of Police and the Attorney-General of the Federation. The suspect was arrested in Ekiti State and allegedly confessed to the offence. Ezima urged members of the public to verify the identities of individuals who contact them while claiming to be police officers or senior government officials. Suspect arrested over alleged property theft The AIG also disclosed the arrest of 40-year-old Paulsurplus Yohanna from Paiko Local Government Area of Niger State over the alleged theft and attempted sale of land documents and other property belonging to his former employer. Yohanna, an employee of a foreign national resident in Abuja, was arrested on August 13 following intelligence received by the NPF-NCCC. According to Ezima, several land title documents allegedly belonging to the suspect’s former employer were recovered from him at the time of his arrest. Preliminary investigation allegedly showed that the suspect was disengaged from his employment in January 2026 and subsequently sold one of the properties in the Kagini area of Abuja. The police also alleged that the suspect duplicated a key to his former employer’s office, forged some land documents and sold a Toyota RAV4 belonging to his employer for N25 million. Ezima said operatives had commenced efforts to trace and recover the proceeds of the alleged transactions and identify other properties and documents allegedly taken by the suspect. He said the suspect remained in police custody as investigations continued to determine the full extent of the alleged offences and identify other persons who may have participated in or benefited from the transactions. Police warn cybercriminals Ezima warned cybercriminals that the use of encrypted platforms, cryptocurrency or false identities would not shield them from investigation and prosecution. “The long arm of the law will catch up with you,” he warned. He said the NPF-NCCC was strengthening its technical capabilities and international partnerships to identify, trace and prosecute individuals involved in cyber-enabled crimes. The suspects in the various cases are expected to face prosecution under the Cybercrimes Act and other applicable laws upon the conclusion of investigations. The post Police bust cybercrime syndicates over N3.62bn investment fraud, romance scams appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Rivers council chairman blasts NBA over VDM invitation
items.description: … Calls for stronger engagement on electoral law By Daniel Abia, Port Harcourt The Chairman of Emohua Local Government Area of Rivers State, Dr Chidi Julius Lloyd, has criticised the Nigerian Bar Association (NBA) over the invitation of social media personality Martins Vincent Otse, popularly known as VeryDarkMan (VDM), to speak at its ongoing 66th Annual General Conference in Port Harcourt. Lloyd, a former law lecturer at the University of Nigeria, Enugu Campus, described the invitation as inappropriate, arguing that the NBA’s annual conference should prioritise serious legal discourse and issues affecting Nigeria’s justice and democratic systems. He spoke in an interview with our correspondent on Wednesday, following VDM’s appearance at one of the sessions of the conference. In a statement posted on his Facebook page and titled, “Shame on the NBA,” Lloyd said the association should remain focused on promoting legal excellence, professional ethics, constitutionalism and national development. He said the NBA had historically served as a platform for legal practitioners, jurists and advocates of the rule of law to engage on critical national issues. “It is therefore deeply disappointing that the NBA Annual Conference, which should feature renowned legal luminaries, senior advocates, judges and policy experts, is now being reduced to an avenue for clout, content creation and social media theatrics,” he said. Lloyd particularly objected to what he described as attacks on security agencies during VDM’s appearance at the conference, saying members of the Armed Forces deserved respect for their service to the country. “Inviting personalities like VDM to a platform meant for serious legal discourse, and allowing the use of that stage to insult members of the Armed Forces who risk their lives daily for our territorial sovereignty, was a misplacement of priority,” he said. “The military deserves respect, not blackmail on a Bar platform. Kudos to the two officers who stood up and responded. That was a defence of dignity and service.” The council chairman urged the NBA to return its focus to what he described as its core responsibilities of scholarship, advocacy, discipline and nation-building. “The Bar cannot afford to trade gravitas for virality. The legal profession deserves better. Nigeria deserves better,” he said. Lloyd also questioned the composition of the conference’s speakers, expressing disappointment that Senate President Godswill Akpabio, Speaker of the House of Representatives Tajudeen Abbas and Attorney-General of the Federation and Minister of Justice, Lateef Fagbemi, SAN, were not invited to speak at the event. He argued that the conference provided an opportunity for robust discussion of electoral reforms and other issues affecting Nigeria’s democratic development. Rather than what he described as “tantrums” at the conference, Lloyd urged the NBA to facilitate substantive engagement on electoral law and other matters of national importance. He also criticised the invitation of Labour Party presidential candidate in the 2023 election, Peter Obi, to the conference, questioning his record on local government elections while he was governor of Anambra State. “It is a shame that Peter Obi, who did not care to conduct a local government election in Anambra State for the eight years he was governor, was also invited to the conference to express his political interest,” Lloyd said. The post Rivers council chairman blasts NBA over VDM invitation appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Gaz naturel : l’Algérie se penche sur le dossier de sa consommation interne
items.description: La consommation de gaz naturel en Algérie a fait l’objet d’une réunion au sommet du secteur des hydrocarbures et de l’énergie ce mercredi 26 août. Dans un contexte marqué par la hausse de la consommation de l’électricité qui a battu des records cette année en raison de la canicule et de celle du gaz naturel , les ministres des Hydrocarbures, Mohamed Arkab, et de l'Énergie et des Énergies renouvelables, Mourad Adjal, ont tenu une réunion de coordination ce mercredi. Le PDG de Sonatrach, Noureddine Daoudi, était présent. Au menu : la gestion de la demande des « grands consommateurs de gaz en Algérie », a indiqué le ministère de l'Énergie. Consommation de gaz en Algérie : deux contraintes majeures Cette réunion, tenue au siège du ministère de l'Énergie et des Énergies renouvelables en présence de cadres des deux départements ministériels, a été consacrée à l'examen du « dossier de la gestion de la demande des grands consommateurs d'énergie gazière à l'échelle nationale, en tant que dossier stratégique de développement contribuant au renforcement de l'efficacité des politiques publiques en matière d'énergie et de rationalisation de sa consommation », précise la même source. Le ministère des Hydrocarbures a indiqué que la gestion de la demande des grands consommateurs de gaz au niveau national est un « dossier stratégique » de développement contribuant au « renforcement de l'efficacité des politiques publiques relatives à l'énergie et à la rationalisation de sa consommation ». Les trois hauts dirigeants du secteur de l’énergie ont échangé sur deux contraintes majeures. La première concerne les « moyens possibles d'améliorer les indicateurs d'efficacité énergétique ». La seconde est d'assurer une « utilisation optimale des ressources énergétiques nationales, en cohérence avec les exigences du développement économique et social durable, tout en renforçant la sécurité énergétique à moyen et long terme ». L’Algérie produit plus de 100 milliards de m³ de gaz par an. Elle consomme la moitié et exporte l’autre. La consommation intérieure de cette énergie ne cesse d’augmenter en raison du lancement de nouveaux investissements dans le domaine de la sidérurgie et de la pétrochimie, de l’extension du réseau d’alimentation en gaz naturel des populations et de la hausse de la consommation de l’électricité qui est produite majoritairement grâce au gaz naturel. « Si l’Algérie continue à exploiter son gaz en l’exportant et en le consommant au niveau national, nous en avons pour 24 ans », a indiqué en janvier dernier l’ancien ministre de l’Énergie, Sadek Boussena. L’article Gaz naturel : l'Algérie se penche sur le dossier de sa consommation interne est apparu en premier sur TSA .

items.title: Gov Sule orders arrest, prosecution of health workers over alleged sale of hospital equipment
items.description: By Edwin Phillip, Lafia Governor Abdullahi Sule of Nasarawa State has ordered the arrest and prosecution of health workers allegedly involved in the sale of hospital equipment donated to a health facility in Umaisha Development Area of the state. Sule described the alleged sale of the equipment as a serious act of misconduct and corruption, stressing that such actions amounted to a lack of concern for patients and the healthcare needs of residents. The governor gave the directive on Wednesday during the inauguration of eight commissioners, special advisers, permanent secretaries and board members at the Aliyu Akwe Doma Banquet Hall, Government House, Lafia. He also charged the newly appointed officials to uphold prudence, fairness, transparency, professionalism and accountability in the discharge of their responsibilities. Sule said he had directed the Commissioner for Health, Dr Gaza Gwamna, to investigate the matter and ensure that those found responsible were brought to justice. He said the equipment had been donated by the member representing Umaisha/Ugya Constituency in the Nasarawa State House of Assembly, Ibrahim Abdullahi Sa’ad, who purchased them with his personal funds to improve conditions at the health facility. According to the governor, the lawmaker recently provided mattresses, ceiling fans and standing fans after becoming concerned about the condition of the primary healthcare facility. “A very honourable member from Umaisha/Ugya recently bought a lot of mattresses and all kinds of fans, standing fans, ceiling fans and the rest of that because he was concerned about what his local primary healthcare was undergoing,” Sule said. He, however, said the lawmaker later returned to the facility and discovered that the donated items could not be accounted for. “Few days back, he returned there and discovered that the officials of the hospital had actually sold those items. This is a terrible thing that will happen if you have people who do not mean well for Nasarawa State,” he said. Sule said he expected the Commissioner for Health to submit a report on the matter by the end of the week. “I am waiting for the honourable commissioner, and I expect that report by the end of this week,” the governor added. The governor’s directive followed a confrontation on Monday between Sa’ad and staff of General Hospital, Umaisha, over equipment he said he donated to the facility. In a video of the encounter that circulated on social media, the visibly angry lawmaker questioned hospital officials over the whereabouts of 50 orthopaedic mattresses, more than 50 ceiling fans and about 40 standing fans he said he purchased for patients at the facility. “Doctor, you remember the last time I spoke with you about those orthopaedic mattresses? You remember what you told me? For Allah’s sake, don’t allow me to get upset,” Sa’ad was heard saying. He also demanded an explanation over the missing electrical appliances. “Where are the ceiling fans? Where are the ceiling fans? I bought more than 50 ceiling fans. The standing fans, I bought about 40. Where are they?” he asked. The lawmaker expressed concern over the condition of patients at the hospital and demanded to see the mattresses, following reports that they were being moved between wards. The governor’s directive is expected to be followed by an investigation by the state Ministry of Health to determine what happened to the donated equipment and establish responsibility for any alleged wrongdoing. OSP has saved Ghana over 20 times the resources invested in it – Kissi Agyebeng
items.description: Special Prosecutor Kissi Agyebeng says the Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has saved the state more than 20 times the total resources allocated to it since its establishment. Addressing a press briefing, he said the financial savings, alongside a number of institutional reforms and interventions, provide measurable evidence of the OSP’s contribution to Ghana’s fight against corruption. “The OSP has saved the nation more than twentyfold the total amount of money released to it since its establishment, and it has thereby fully paid for and far above the resources invested in it,” he said on Wednesday, August 26. Mr Agyabeng said the OSP had secured financial recoveries of GH¢8.5 million and US$2 million, in addition to movable and immovable assets linked to ongoing recovery proceedings. According to him, the OSP’s interventions have extended beyond prosecutions to protecting state assets, improving revenue mobilisation and plugging leakages in government systems. He cited the OSP’s intervention at the Tema Oil Refinery (TOR), saying the office helped prevent the refinery from being “pawned off” and contributed to its return to operation after years of inactivity. Mr Agyebeng also pointed to the OSP’s work in the customs sector, which he said had resulted in a “more robust system for auctioning seized items and a significant reduction in the abuse of the Customs Advanced Ruling regime.” He said these interventions were aimed at ensuring that the state recoups more revenue that could otherwise have been lost. The Special Prosecutor further highlighted the OSP’s intervention in the government payroll system, which he said had so far saved the country a little over GH¢100 million. “The OSP’s shake-up of the government payroll system has saved the nation a little over a hundred million cedis so far,” he stated. Mr Agyebeng argued that when these savings and other financial benefits are considered against the resources invested in the institution, the OSP has more than justified its cost. His comments form part of a broader defence of the OSP’s record amid calls by some critics for the institution to be scrapped or for its operations to be significantly restructured.

items.title: Kwabena Donkor, four others named as persons of interest in Asante Berko case – OSP
items.description: The Office of the Special Prosecutor (OSP) has named former Power Minister Kwabena Donkor and four other individuals as its main persons of interest in its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension of the Asante Kweku Berko bribery case. The other named individuals are Francis Walkson Kwesi Gyata, a former technical adviser to the Minister of Power; Solomon Adjetey Sowah, a former deputy director at the Ministry of Power; Lindin George Nii Mettle, a former director at Tricop Group Limited; and Baffour Ankomah Brobbey, an employee of Tricop Group Limited. Special Prosecutor Kissi Agyebeng disclosed this at a press conference while providing an update on the OSP’s investigation into the case. The development follows the conviction of Asante Kweku Berko by a federal jury in Brooklyn, New York, on August 3, 2026, over a bribery scheme involving more than US$1 million. Berko, a dual citizen of Ghana and the United States and a former managing director of the Tema Oil Refinery, was convicted over allegations that he conspired to pay bribes to multiple Ghanaian officials between 2014 and 2015. The alleged payments were linked to the development and financing of a 370-megawatt fuel oil plant in Tema under an agreement involving the Republic of Ghana, Turkish energy company AXA Energy Eratim and Goldman Sachs. Mr Agyebeng said the OSP provided investigative and evidentiary assistance to the US Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) through Ghana’s mutual legal assistance framework. He said the US Department of Justice had acknowledged the OSP’s assistance in the successful prosecution. OSP cautions against equating ‘person of interest’ with suspect The Special Prosecutor stressed that the five individuals named should not automatically be considered suspects. “Please bear in mind and this point should be strongly emphasised: that the person of interest is not necessarily a suspect,” he said. He explained that the two classifications have different meanings in an investigation and should not be treated as interchangeable. Mr Agyebeng further cautioned that being identified as a person of interest does not amount to a finding of criminal liability. “Identification in either category does not constitute criminal culpability or conviction until guilt is proved beyond reasonable doubt to the satisfaction of a court of competent jurisdiction,” he said. He said other persons of interest include some present and former employees of the Volta River Authority, Ghana Grid Company Limited, Electricity Company of Ghana, Public Utilities Regulatory Commission and some staff of the former Ministry of Power. The OSP said its investigation into the Ghanaian dimension remains ongoing. Mr Agyebeng explained that Berko’s conviction in the United States does not automatically provide grounds for prosecuting other individuals in Ghana. He said each person’s conduct must be assessed under Ghanaian law and supported by lawfully obtained evidence capable of sustaining a prosecution. “The OSP will not prosecute the person solely on the basis that the person’s name appears in proceedings conducted in another country,” he said. He added, however, that the OSP would prosecute any person where the evidence establishes a proper basis for doing so.
